d4ca6ef76ef1: Salesforce Timeline View: Every Resource on One Screen
647e3d1f6897: A Salesforce resource timeline: rooms, people and equipment down the side, dates across, multi-day bookings as one bar, and drag to reschedule. No code.
23f0ad57eedb: Does Salesforce have a timeline view for resources?
8d815844b90e: Not as a standard Lightning component for your own objects. Calendars in Salesforce show one person's events, and Gantt-style charts usually mean an add-on built for projects. MultiDatePick adds a resource timeline that reads any custom or standard object: pick the object that holds bookings and the object that holds resources, and every resource becomes a row.
624d77150319: Can I drag bookings on the timeline to reschedule them?
3eb7176acb93: Yes. With Edit Mode on, grab the middle of a bar to move it to other days or either edge to change its start or end. The bar shows its new dates while you drag and saves when you let go. In Day zoom the same gestures move and stretch the booking's start and end times.
03121cffd8ba: Can the rows be people instead of rooms?
6dd7427fb64d: Yes. The resource can be any object, including User. Point it at User and the timeline becomes a staff roster: each person a row, their shifts, visits or assignments as bars.
ccaada97f9b0: How do I stop a long list of resources turning into a wall of rows?
5c6178c7887c: Set Max View Resources to draw only the busiest rows, group rows under a picklist or lookup with Timeline Group By Field, and choose whether rows show all resources or only ones with bookings. Every resource still counts toward capacity; the settings only change what is drawn.
38c51173abaf: Does the timeline work on Experience Cloud sites and record pages?
ae7cb6e730c7: Yes. It is one of five views in the same component, so it runs anywhere the component does: record pages, app and home pages, Flow screens and Experience Cloud sites.

3b5a25093d3a: Rooms, people, equipment or projects down the side, dates across the top, and every booking drawn as one bar. A resource timeline for any Salesforce object, set up without code.
0e99a13be1bc: "Which room is free next Tuesday?" "Who on the team has capacity this week?" "When does the van come back?" Each of those is a question about many resources across many days, and a month calendar answers it one resource at a time. A timeline answers it in one look.
fb816ce9d43c: MultiDatePick's Timeline view puts every resource on its own row and every booking on a bar that runs exactly as long as the booking does. It reads your own Salesforce objects, saves through the same path as the rest of the component, and is one config field away from any placement.
89264722c76d: Advisors down the side, engagements as bars, zoom from a week to a month. Hover any bar for its details.

30a9fd912166: A booking that runs Monday to Friday is one continuous bar, so its length is visible at a glance.
3001fa64d289: Overlapping bookings on a resource stack into lanes. A busy day collapses to a count you expand in place.
3051e38cb708: A strip above each group shows how full every day is against the resources' combined capacity.
701d1327e982: Hours across for today, two weeks for planning, a month for the long view. One click between them.

0a545b7dd134: Drag to reschedule, stretch to extend
fca8b459bb7b: Plans change, and changing one should not mean opening a record, editing two date fields and saving. On the timeline you grab the bar. Pull its right edge and the booking runs longer; grab the middle and it slides to other days. The bar shows the dates it will land on while you drag, saves the moment you let go, and stays in its lane with a brief highlight so you can see exactly what changed.
2621b6f6958c: Stretch from the edge, slide from the middle. Each change saves on release.
eb12320c9cd0: Switch to <t1>Day</t1> zoom and the columns become hours. The same gestures then move and stretch a booking's start and end <t2>times</t2>, so a meeting that runs over is one drag to fix.
c37fe7c384fe: Capacity you can see at a glance
d8c93fca5af1: Above the rows, a capacity strip shades every day by how much of the resources' combined capacity is booked, so the crunch weeks stand out before anyone asks. Group rows by a picklist or lookup (building, team, region) and each group gets its own strip. When one resource has several bookings on the same day, they stack into lanes; a day with more than a few collapses to a count that expands in place when you click it.
